title: K-injective targets compute enhanced derived mapping complexes
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $E$ be a small category, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}(E,\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda})$, with morphisms the natural transformations. This includes $\Lambda$-modules when $E$ is the one-object identity category, and module presheaves when $E=\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Use unbounded cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The differential graded category $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)$ has global product Hom complex
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}^r(A,B)=\prod_{k\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(A^k,B^{k+r}),\qquad d(h)=d_Bh-(-1)^rh d_A,$$
with composition the composition of graded maps. Write $q:\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)\to\mathbf D_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal A)$ for its enhanced localization at quasi-isomorphisms [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], retaining derived mapping complexes and all composition homotopies. A complex $J$ is K-injective when $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}^{\bullet}(B,J)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $B$; acyclic means that every cohomology object is zero.

For every complex $A$ and every K-injective complex $J$, the canonical localization map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}^{\bullet}(A,J)\longrightarrow\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(qA,qJ)$$
is an equivalence in the derived category of abelian groups (equivalently, a quasi-isomorphism in a complex presentation), where the right side is the mapping object of $\mathbf D_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal A)$ in the derived category of abelian groups. It is natural in chain maps in $A$ and in K-injective targets $J$, compatible with shifts and with composition whenever the relevant targets are K-injective. Source quasi-isomorphisms and quasi-isomorphisms of K-injective targets are inverted by this comparison. On localization in these variables it remains a coherent natural equivalence compatible with composition and its higher homotopies. No boundedness of either complex is assumed.

The comparison of entire mapping complexes and its enriched coherence are the agent-extracted enhancement of the retained dense-comparison proof, former step 6; they are not attributed to the ordinary Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal A$ are computed at every object of $E$, with the structure maps induced by naturality. Hence cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms are objectwise. All the products in the stated Hom complex exist as products of abelian groups in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]; these are global natural transformations, not objectwise Hom groups. We use the shift convention $(J[n])^k=J^{k+n}$, $d_{J[n]}=(-1)^nd_J$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: Directly from the displayed Hom differential, $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,J[n])=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,J)[n]$ after reindexing. Thus $J[n]$ is K-injective for every integer $n$. A degree-$n$ cocycle $h$ in $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,J)$ satisfies $d_Jh=(-1)^nhd_A$, exactly the chain-map equation for $A\to J[n]$. If $h=d(k)$, then the degree-minus-one map $(-1)^nk:A\to J[n]$ has $d_{J[n]}((-1)^nk)+((-1)^nk)d_A=h$; conversely every null homotopy has this form. Therefore $H^n\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,J)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,J[n])$, naturally for chain maps.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: For a source quasi-isomorphism $s:A'\to A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to the K-injective target $J[n]$. Under the two bijections in its statement, the map on the groups of step 2 is precomposition by the invertible derived morphism $Qs$. It is bijective for every $n$. The comparison squares commute because localization preserves composition. Thus $s^*:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,J)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A',J)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, by the definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: If $t:J\to J'$ is a quasi-isomorphism of K-injective complexes, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes it a chain homotopy equivalence. Choose a chain homotopy inverse $u$. Postcomposition by $t,u$ gives inverse maps up to chain homotopy on $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,-)$: a degree-minus-one homotopy $v$ with $dv+vd=ut-1$ induces $h\mapsto vh$, and the Hom differential gives $d(vh)+v(dh)=(ut-1)h$. The same calculation applies to $tu-1$. These maps therefore induce inverse maps on every cohomology group, so postcomposition by $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: Define a small dg category $\mathcal B$ with objects those of $E$, with $\mathcal B(U,V)=\Lambda[\operatorname{Hom}_E(V,U)]$ in degree zero, zero differential, and composition induced by composition in $E$ and multiplication in $\Lambda$. Right dg $\mathcal B$-modules are precisely complexes in $\mathcal A$: the action of the basis arrow corresponding to $U\to V$ is the structure map $M(U)\to M(V)$, and the scalar endomorphisms give the $\Lambda$-module structure. Conversely extend these actions linearly. The two constructions are inverse. Degree-$r$ module maps are exactly families of natural $\Lambda$-linear maps $A^k\to J^{k+r}$; thus the Hom complexes, their differentials and compositions agree exactly. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] to obtain, for any $A$, a quasi-isomorphism $p:PA\to A$ with $PA$ homotopically projective. Its statement says that the canonical comparison $c_{PA,J}:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(PA,J)\to\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(qPA,qJ)$ is an equivalence, compatible with localization. The identification is with the enhanced localization in this item by the universal property [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal].

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: Let $c_{A,J}$ be the canonical map on mapping objects induced by the enriched localization functor $q$. Functoriality of $q$ gives the square with horizontal arrows $c_{A,J}$ and $c_{PA,J}$ and vertical arrows $p^*$ on ordinary Hom and precomposition by $qp$ on derived Hom. The left vertical arrow is an equivalence by step 3, the right vertical arrow is an equivalence because $qp$ is invertible, and the lower horizontal arrow is an equivalence by step 5. Thus $c_{A,J}$ is an equivalence in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. This proves the entire mapping-object comparison, using an actual map of mapping objects; it does not reconstruct a map merely from isomorphisms on cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: The maps $c$ are the mapping maps of the single enriched functor $q$. They therefore form an enriched natural transformation in both variables. For composable graded maps $h,g$, their composition compatibility is exactly $q(g\circ h)=q(g)\circ q(h)$, with the composition coherence belonging to that enriched functor. Restrict the middle and final objects to K-injectives so that all three mapping comparisons concerned are equivalences by step 6. Shifts are also compatible: target shifts use the reindexing of step 2; for source shifts the chain isomorphism $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A[k],J)^r\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,J)[-k]^r$ sends $h$ to the family $(-1)^{kr}h^{q-k}$ in component $q$. The $d_J$ terms on both sides have sign $(-1)^{kr+k}$ and the $hd_A$ terms sign $-(-1)^{kr+r}$. A shifted homotopically projective replacement is homotopically projective, since its Hom into an acyclic complex is a shift of an acyclic Hom complex by this formula. Thus step 5 computes the shifted comparison with this same reindexing and sign, proving the shift square for the canonical map.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent-written all-degree and enhanced argument, using the existing dg-module projective presentation and enriched localization statements

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be the full dg subcategory of K-injective complexes, equipped with its quasi-isomorphisms. Steps 3 and 4 show that the Hom bifunctor on $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal I$, interpreted in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, inverts the specified maps in each variable. The derived mapping bifunctor does so by definition, and $c$ is their enriched natural transformation. Apply the multivariable clause of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] to extend these bifunctors and $c$ along the two localizations. Its componentwise equivalence criterion and step 6 make the extended $c$ an equivalence. Apply also its substitution and coherent-diagram clauses to the composition, identity and shift diagrams of step 7. Their already specified homotopies extend, including all higher homotopies, rather than being chosen anew after localization. Every argument used all integer degrees and arbitrary products; no bound or termwise injectivity assumption was used.
